posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
I believe I have stumbled across something beautiful and would like to confirm that I have played it correctly.

The Chairman is in play, and has been flipped. Writhe is in play, and has his Caliginous Form card active. Writhe inflicts damage on the Chairman. The Chairman retaliates for 3 HP of damage. Caliginous Form reduces that to 1 HP and redirects it to the Chairman, who currently the highest-HP villain. Then, because he has been damaged by a target that so happens to be himself, he retaliates and inflicts another 3 HP of damage on himself.

Does that sound right?

posts.name: Ronway
posts.cooked:
McBehrer:

No, that sounds right to me. It's the first time each target hits him, just like backlash field, flame barrier, and combat stance.

The first time The Chairman is dealt damage each turn, deal the source of the damage x melee damage.
The first time Ra is dealt damage by a target each turn, Ra deals tha target 2 fire damage.
Argent Adept allows Ra to use a power, he burns The Chairman for some fire damage. The Chairman hits Ra back since it is the first time The Chairman was dealt damage. Now that Ra was dealt damage for the first time this turn by a target, Ra deals The Chairman 2 fire damage.

Argent Adept then allows Haka to play Rampage. It deals The Chairman 5 melee damage. This is not the first time The Chairman has been dealt damage, thus no damage dealt back to Haka. Haka then hits heroes for 2 damage, which includes Ra. This is the first time Ra has been dealt damage by the target, Haka now takes 2 fire damage.

Different triggers.
